rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead emerge at resurrection as plants emerge when rain revives a dead land: the earth splits and they come out.
rows.anchor: تشققت وخرج منها النبات كذلك تشقق ويخرج منها الأموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording supports reading الرجْع in 50:3 as return (intransitive): if they denied extraction, the fitting answer would have said إخراج, but it says خروج.
rows.anchor: لأنه تعالى بين لهم ما استبعدوه فلو استبعدوا الرجع الذي هو من المتعدي لناسب أن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, extraction and خروج are cause and effect: denying the cause entails denying the effect, so God emphatically affirms the effect after they denied both.
rows.anchor: ووجهها هو أن الرجع والإخراج كالسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From noble character, the Prophet blamed his own shortcoming for their unbelief and therefore intensified his warning and conveying of the message.
rows.anchor: هذه تسلية أخرى ، وذلك لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان من كرم الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reassures the Prophet that he fulfilled his duty; their rejection is not his fault, and their turning away and stubbornness make them culpable.
rows.anchor: قد أتيت بما عليك ، ولا يضرك التولي عنهم ، وكفرهم ليس لتقصير منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation: whoever chose a desired deity in worldly life will be punished here or, if not here, in the afterlife; 53:26 confirms that no intercession will avail.
rows.anchor: يعاقبه على فعله في الدنيا وإن لم يعاقبه في الدنيا فيعاقبه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation: since al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā rest on conjecture and desire, God's ownership shows idols have no authority; 53:26 answers the claim that they are angelic intercessors.
rows.anchor: هذه الأصنام ليس لها من الأمر شيء فكيف يجوز الإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This may console the Prophet, who had explained his mission and God's unity without being believed: the deniers cannot escape God's power.
rows.anchor: هذه تسلية كأنه تعالى قال ذلك لنبيه حيث بين رسالته ووحدانية الله ولم يؤمنوا فقال لا تأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may be a conclusion from proof: after establishing Muhammad's revelation, including the message of divine unity, God's ownership of both lives confirms his truthful report of resurrection.
rows.anchor: بقوله { إن هو إلا وحى يوحى } ( النجم : 4 ) إلى آخره وبين بعض ما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may answer unbelievers who said believers were not better guided because they lacked worldly wealth: God gives wealth and guidance to whom He wills in either life.
rows.anchor: فقال تعالى : إن الله اختار لكم الدنيا وأعطاكم الأموال ولم يعط المؤمنين بعض ذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ākhirah modifies either life or abode; al-ākhir is an active participle from an unattested verb, illustrated by أخرته فتأخر, though usage bars the expected form.
rows.anchor: صفة الحياة أو صفة الدار وهي اسم فاعل من فعل غير مستعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ūlā is the feminine form فعلى, so its masculine أول is an أفعل adjective.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : { الاولى } فعلى للتأنيث ، فالأول إذن أفعل صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every أفعل/فعلى pair requires a base; here, as with الآخر, that source form is unattested.
rows.anchor: كل فعلى وأفعل للتأنيث والتذكير له أصل فليؤخذ منه كالفضلى والأفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A past action is only truly past when complete; a hypothetical verb yielding آخر would mean reaching completed finality, although every completed action has an end after it.
rows.anchor: كل فعل مستعمل فله آخر ، وذلك لأن له ماضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form تأخر is a reflexive or effortful claim to being last, not proof of a basic verb that makes someone truly آخر.
rows.anchor: وزن الفعل ينادي على صحة ما ذكرنا فإنه من باب التكلف والتكبر إذا استعمل في غير المتكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آخر is an active participle without a verb, intensified as أفعل; آخر is a connected part, while الآخر is separate and comes after it.
rows.anchor: الآخر فاعل ليس له فعل ، ومبالغته بأفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأول has neither a verb nor a participle: an agent must precede an act, so the first cannot itself derive from an act that makes it first.
rows.anchor: فإذا الفاعل أولا ثم الفعل ، فإذا كان الفاعل أول الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent counterexample from سبق fails: سابق applied to the first is resemblance, since an agent and its act do not compete; تقدم was already answered through تأخر.
rows.anchor: الفاعل والفعل لا يتسابقان فالفاعل لا يسبقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects deriving أول from آل as “making another first” as far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وما يقال إن أول بمعنى جعل الآخر أولا لاستخراج معنى من الكلام فبعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أول and آخر are أفعل/فاعل forms, whereas قبل and بعد are neither forms; the words therefore differ morphologically even when their senses are related.
rows.anchor: فإن الآخر فاعل من غير فعل والأول أفعل من غير فاعل ولا فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آخر requires a specific afterness with nothing further after it; something can follow the first yet remain intermediate rather than last.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده أن الآخر لا يتحقق إلا ببعدية مخصوصة وهي التي لا بعدية بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relation is asymmetrical: arriving after everyone explains why someone is last, but being last does not explain every use of “after.”
rows.anchor: ولا تعكسه فتقول هذا آخر من جاء لأنه جاء بعد الكل ولا تقول هو جاء بعد الكل لأنه آخر من جاء

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Rāzī cites the Prophet's saying, “Do not revile time, for time is God”; he gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لا تسبوا الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Temporal priority and posteriority have reality only through God; without God there would be no temporal order to revile.
rows.anchor: والبعدية والقبلية حقيقة لإثبات الله ولا مفهوم للزمان إلا ما به القبلية والبعدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Arabs use الأولة as feminine of الأول, أولى looks like a comparative whose feminine should not take ة; أول is exceptional, resembling both أربع/أرنب and الأكبر/الأصغر, so أولى is also used.
rows.anchor: أول لما كان أفعل وليس له فاعل شابه الأربع والأرنب فجاز إلحاق التاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms الأولة and الأولى explain why أولا may appear with or without tanwin: the ة form permits it, while الأولى is diptote.
rows.anchor: فمن قال بأن تأنيث أول أولة فهو كالأربع والأربعة فجاز التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾanic feminine الأولى is more common, so the usual form leaves tanwin; Arabs also preserve the etymological أولة, though Rāzī calls it weaker.
rows.anchor: الأشهر ترك التنوين لأن الأشهر أن تأنيثه أولى وعليه استعمال القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further grammatical proposal is that أفعل is diptote only when its feminine is exclusively فعلى; allowing a ة feminine removes that restriction.
rows.anchor: منع الصرف من أفعل لا يكون إلا إذا لم يكن تأنيثه إلا فعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين is most likely بدل of الذين أحسنوا: God recompenses evil-doers and good-doers, and the good-doers are those who avoid major sins and receive the best reward.
rows.anchor: الذين يحتمل أن يكون بدلا عن الذين أحسنوا وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the good-doer does not benefit God; avoiding evil defines the praised good-doer, while one who commits major sins is an evil-doer.
rows.anchor: ويتبين به أن المحسن ليس ينفع الله بإحسانه شيئا وهو الذي لا يسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone performing voluntary devotions exceeds the defined rank of muḥsin; since God promises muḥsins an increase, those above them receive multiplied rewards.
rows.anchor: فالذي يأتي بالنوافل يكون فوق المحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this begins a new sentence: God forgives those who avoid major sins, as the following statement about His ample forgiveness indicates.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ابتداء كلام تقديره الذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم يغفر الله لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the new-sentence reading, the passage distinguishes wrongdoers, good-doers, and people who neither sinned nor performed good deeds, such as children not yet accountable; their reward is below the best reward.
rows.anchor: وحال من لم يحسن ولم يسيء وهم الذين لم يرتكبوا سيئة وإن لم تصدر منهم الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense denotes a settled habit of avoiding sins, rather than someone who avoided them once but later returned to them, as in saying that habitual visitors asked and were given.
rows.anchor: أي الذين عادتهم ودأبهم الاجتناب لا الذين اجتنبوا مرة وقدموا عليها أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense for avoiding sins stresses repeated, continuing restraint because sins have many kinds; 42:37 likewise uses it for avoiding major sins.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل : في كثير من المواضع قال في الكبائر { والذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast, 39:17 uses the past for avoiding idols: repudiating idolatrous belief is lasting and unitary, whereas particular sins fluctuate and require renewed avoidance.
rows.anchor: وقال في عباد الطاغوت : { والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كبائر is a feminine adjective whose implied noun is sinful acts: “the great acts of sin.”
rows.anchor: نقول : هي صفة الفعلة كأنه يقول : الفعلات الكبائر من الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds cannot be great beside the gratitude owed for God's countless favors; a servant's sin is weighty, though God forgives and lightens some sins.
rows.anchor: الحسنة لا تكون كبيرة لأنها إذا قوبلت بما يجب أن يوجد من العبد في مقابلة نعم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كبائر marks the magnitude of a sin, while فواحش marks the conspicuous degree of its ugliness: quantity versus quality.
rows.anchor: الكبائر إشارة إلى ما فيها من مقدار السيئة ، والفواحش إشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, فاحش is manifestly repugnant; Rāzī adduces the root's permutations and the usage فحشت الناقة for a camel's conspicuous posture while urinating.
rows.anchor: والفاحش في اللغة مختص بالقبيح الخارج قبحه عن حد الخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كبائر needs the qualifier الإثم to identify what is great; فواحش already conveys ugliness, so the verse does not add “of sin” to it.
rows.anchor: ولهذا لم يقل : الفواحش من الإثم وقال في الكبائر : { كبائر الإثم }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One definition makes major sins those for which God explicitly and plainly threatens hell, and obscenities those carrying a worldly prescribed penalty.
rows.anchor: فقيل : الكبائر ما أوعد الله عليه بالنار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another definition says major sins are those whose permissibility would make the person who deems them lawful an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الكبائر ما يكفر مستحله

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilite definition is that a major sin is not forgiven for its perpetrator until repentance.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الكبائر مالا يغفر الله لفاعله إلا بعد التوبة وهو على مذهب المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects these definitions as explaining an unclear term with an equally or more obscure one; he instead defines major by magnitude and obscene by quality.
rows.anchor: كل هذه التعريفات تعريف الشيء بما هو مثله في الخفاء أو فوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In principle every disobedience is major relative to God's immense favors; God exempts error and forgetfulness because they do not indicate disregard for reverence, given their prevalence or frequent occurrence.
rows.anchor: إن الأصل في كل معصية أن تكون كبيرة ، لأن نعم الله كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An occasional lie or slander, a glance, or an ambiguous offense may be treated as minor because few people in any era avoid such acts altogether.
rows.anchor: كالكذبة والغيبة مرة أو مرتين والنظرة والقبائح التي فيها شبهة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Rāzī's companions say listening to music with string instruments makes one openly sinful, while listening in a town whose people do not take the matter seriously does not.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا : إن استماع الغناء الذي مع الأوتار يفسق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sin is minor when sensible people in its context do not judge its agent to have abandoned proper reverence; that standard varies with time and person.
rows.anchor: إن العقلاء إن لم يعدوه تاركا للتعظيم لا يكون مرتكبا للكبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same pastime can be major for a pious scholar who chases women or plays excessively, but not for a peddler, seller, or otherwise idle person; playing during prayer time differs from other times.
rows.anchor: تختلف الأمور باختلاف الأوقات والأشخاص فالعالم المتقي إذا كان يتبع النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī concludes that every sin is major except what the accountable person knows or reasonably supposes God has excluded through grace and pardon.
rows.anchor: كل ذنب كبيرة إلا ما علم المكلف أو ظن خروجه بفضل الله وعفوه عن الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view reads اللمم as an intention the believer forms but does not carry out, linking the word to gathering or collecting resolve.
rows.anchor: ما يقصده المؤمن ولا يحققه وهو على هذا القول من لم يلم إذا جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view makes اللمم a sin the believer commits and immediately regrets, like a passing touch of madness; 3:135 supports this through its account of remembering God and seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ما يأتي به المؤمن ويندم في الحال وهو من اللمم الذي هو مس من الجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view takes اللمم as a minor sin, from ألم meaning to alight briefly; ألم بالطعام can mean eating only a little.
rows.anchor: اللمم الصغير من الذنب من ألم إذا نزل نزولا من غير لبث طويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If إلا is an exception from الفواحش, it may be disconnected because اللمم is not itself an obscenity.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع لأن اللمم ليس من الفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may instead be connected: relative to what is due to God, every sin is major and obscene, but God exempts some offenses and promises to pardon them.
rows.anchor: غير منقطع لما بينا أن كل معصية إذا نظرت إلى جانب الله تعالى وما يجب أن يكون عليه فهي كبيرة وفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا may mean غير, making the phrase “obscenities other than اللمم”; the force differs according to whether غير distinguishes a class or merely emphasizes and clarifies.
rows.anchor: ثانيها : { إلا } بمعنى غير وتقديره والفواحش غير اللمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse makes the exception attach to the implied action in يجتنبون: they avoid sins except for approaching them without actually committing them, which is اللمم.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : هو استثناء من الفعل الذي يدل عليه قوله تعالى : { الذين يجتنبون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ample forgiveness fits both readings: good-doers are rewarded, avoiders of major sins are forgiven minor ones, and major sinners who repent are forgiven; persistent wrongdoers remain outside forgiveness.
rows.anchor: المحسن مجزى وذنبه مغفور ، ومجتنب الكبائر كذلك ذنبه الصغير مغفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's withholding forgiveness from persistent wrongdoers reflects His will, not any limit in its capacity: He could forgive everyone who does good and evil.
rows.anchor: بين أن ذلك ليس لضيق فيها ، بل ذلك بمشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مغفرة means covering; measured against God's blessings, every creature falls short, so each needs its deeds covered, even one who repays an unstinting benefactor only a dirham or less.
rows.anchor: والمغفرة من الستر ، وهو لا يكون إلا على قبيح ، وكل من خلقه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God knows people from their creation may reinforce 53:30: secret nighttime acts are no more hidden than the conditions of embryos in their mothers' wombs.
rows.anchor: أحدها : هو تقرير لما مر من قوله : { هو أعلم بمن ضل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation links guidance and misguidance to divine decree: God knew their states in the wombs and wrote some as misguided and others as guided.
rows.anchor: ثانيها : هو إشارة إلى الضال والمهتدي حصلا على ما هما عليه بتقدير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation connects the verse to recompense in 53:31: God can reassemble each person's scattered bodily parts correctly because He knows them as He created them.
rows.anchor: ثالثها : تأكيد وبيان للجزاء ، وذلك لأنه لما قال : { ليجزى الذين أساءوا بما عملوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذ may be governed by the implied meaning of أعلم: God knew you at the time of your creation.
rows.anchor: العامل في : { إذ } يحتمل أن يكون ما يدل عليه : { أعلم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, إذ is governed by an implied اذكروا: the completed statement says God knows you, then tells doubters to recall their creation from earth.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون اذكروا فيكون تقريرا لكونه عالما

rows.speaker: من الناس
rows.claim: Some take “He created you from the earth” as referring to Adam, who was made from soil.
rows.anchor: من الناس من قال آدم فإنه من تراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says every person originates from earth: earth becomes nourishment and then semen.
rows.anchor: وقررنا أن كل أحد أصله من التراب ، فإنه يصير غذاء ، ثم يصير نطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hypothetical objection says the first creation clause must concern Adam, since the embryo clause concerns other people; making both clauses about everyone would imply that all were embryos in wombs, attributed here to philosophers.
rows.anchor: لو قال قائل : لا بد من صرف { إذ أنشأكم من الأرض } إلى آدم ، لأن { وإذ أنتم أجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that the address concerns those present when spoken; whether it extends to all after the revelation or only its contemporaries, all are from earth and were embryos.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن كل هؤلاء من الأرض وهم كانوا أجنة
